title: Adaptive queue + kernel-throttle emergency patch for cross-tier token throughput regression
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
In the last 36 hours we received multiple escalations from Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers reporting degraded first-token time (TTFT) and overall tokens/sec on production workloads. The regression is most visible on long-context chat flows and multi-tenant inference pools after the kernel-scheduler heuristic change deployed in runtime-1.21.

Symptoms observed:
- Median TTFT for short prompts (<=64 tokens) increased from ~110ms to ~360ms on hosted-small pools (40%+ tail variance).
- Aggregate tokens/sec on quantized 16-bit models dropped ~35% across dedicated GPU pools when concurrent sessions >120.
- Tail latency (p95/p99) increased dramatically for on-prem/private installs that use our adaptive batching knobs.
- Issue surface spans: kernel selection path, the adaptive queue sizing, and backpressure handling for multi-tenant request windows.

Root cause hypothesis (validated by initial triage):
- The kernel-scheduler heuristic change (commit c1a9f3e) aggressively favored large contiguous strides to maximize throughput. Under realistic mixed-size request distributions this caused longer scheduling windows and delayed small prompt dispatch (increased TTFT).
- Combined with tighter KV-cache prefetch gating, small requests now wait behind larger batched work, causing tokens/sec drop and queueing pressure across tenants.

Temporary impact mitigations already applied:
- Rolled out per-tenant soft-rate-limits to reduce head-of-line blocking in hosted pools (temporary, deployed 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC).
- Enabled KV-prefetch bypass for high-priority short requests (hot-path) in two Dedicated pools as a canary.
- Manual routing of top-5 escalated customers to legacy kernel selector that existed pre-c1a9f3e.

Proposed fix (emergency patch):
1) Add a lightweight kernel-throttle guard: if a small-request enters queue and estimated dispatch delay > X ms, preempt previously scheduled large-batch slots and force a small-kernel path.
2) Adaptive queue sizing: dynamically shrink batch windows when short-request frequency rises above threshold, with a cap to avoid throughput loss on sustained large-batch workloads.
3) Backfill token accounting: ensure multi-tenant token-quota accounting honors preempted jobs so quota fairness is preserved.
4) Automated canary rollout: dedicated pool -> hosted canary -> full hosted/dedicated/private. Private installs will receive a patch bundle and clear rollback instructions.

Trade-offs and notes:
- The kernel-throttle guard introduces extra scheduler churn; we expect a small throughput impact (~5-8%) for pure large-batch workloads but TTFT improvements for mixed traffic. This is acceptable given customer impact.
- Longer-term: revert the aggressive stride heuristic and design more granular cost model in kernel selector (tracked separately under runtime-kernel-redesign).

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Median TTFT for short prompts returns to baseline (<=140ms) on canary pools.
- Cluster-wide tokens/sec recovers to within 95% of pre-regression levels for mixed workloads under controlled load tests.
- p99 latency reduces by >=40% for affected tenants in canary before global rollout.

Rollback plan:
- If canary fails acceptance criteria, immediately revert to legacy kernel-selection codepath (automated revert PR ready: GH-rlw/revert-c1a9f3e).
- Communicate to affected customers and keep temporary routing to legacy selector until stable.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver emergency patch PR with feature-flag and unit/integration tests (owner: Miguel). Target PR by 2026-03-12 EOD.
- Run synthetic mixed-workload testbench for dedicated/hotst/priv pools (A/B) and collect TTFT/tokens/sec metrics.
- Coordinate canary rollout with SRE for rollback hooks and extra monitoring (alerting, dashboards).

Longer term:
- Follow-up RFC to revise kernel selection cost model and deploy a non-disruptive migration path.
- Add more detailed request-size telemetry to enable automated throttling policies per customer.
